description: Three held illustrated states, not generated motion; planet -> star system -> local stars; representative enlarged icons and compressed space.

images.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one polished 16:9 cinematic illustrated starting frame for the next music-video shot, not a storyboard collage.
References: image 1 establishes Harper's face identity only (ignore its zoo clothing); image 2 establishes the approved graphic-novel painting, gray clothing, thin cyan geodesic field and amber/dark-metal cabin. Preserve those identities but change the camera angle and pose for this new scene.
Scene: inside her spherical spacecraft. Harper floats in zero gravity, gray short sleeve tee and gray trousers, barefoot, auburn curls, freckles. Three-quarter oblique medium-wide shot viewed from slightly above and beside a spatial hologram, with Harper on the right and the hologram spanning the left/center foreground. Her face and both hands remain unobstructed and anatomically coherent. She concentrates on a fingertip selection; one hand selects a hovering ring while the other prepares a spreading gesture. Warm upper-right sunlight edges her curls, cyan diagram spill lightly illuminates her face and fingertips.
The hologram is a legible volumetric navigation model suspended at chest height, NOT a screen, flat HUD, glass panel, or literal celestial bodies in the cabin. Starting state: a grapefruit-size transparent cyan/turquoise schematic sphere of the same mountainous cloudy world, enlarged far beyond physical scale so its features read. A small amber locator with a stylized ship icon marks her current orbit. Two clearly much smaller diagram moon symbols, a volcanic orange symbol and an icy pale blue symbol, sit on offset fine orbit ellipses. Use sparse fine construction contours and three-dimensional latitude/cross-section cues on the planet, interrupted rings, depth occlusion, subtle diminishing brightness behind the sphere, and a few stable selection nodes. Orbital paths tilt in different planes and are viewed as ellipses, never all as concentric circles face-on. Distances are intentionally compressed and body icons enlarged: an organized representative navigation model, not astronomical scale.
Behind the hologram, a portion of the complete dark satin equatorial band with continuous amber rim and sparse rectangular cyan lights establishes the cabin. Faint curved cyan hexagonal shell lines across space, not heavy opaque glass or a grid cage. Nebula and sparse distant stars behind. NO real background moons in this particular angle: the two tiny schematic moon symbols belong only to the diagram and must be distinct from distant scenery. The hologram itself is cyan/teal with restrained amber highlights, semitransparent and clearly smaller than Harper.
Sparse small invented alien glyphs beside only a few diagram features; no recognizable English, human numerals, subtitles, watermark or logo. Keep the bottom 10% comparatively quiet for later lyrics. Detailed painterly graphic-novel illustration matching reference 2, with realistic anatomy and drawn texture, not photorealism or plastic 3D. Preserve continuity of ship materials, full metal-band geometry and extraordinarily transparent thin field.
PROMPT LOCK: Cinematic painterly graphic-novel space adventure. Harper is the established adult freckled woman with curly auburn hair, gray short-sleeve tee, gray trousers and bare feet. Ship: ultra-thin clear spherical technological field with faint curved cyan geodesic lines, dark satin metal equatorial band and upper/lower circular platforms, continuous amber rim lights, sparse rectangular cyan lamps, one aft vertical open engine ring with cyan inner arc when visible. Background Moon A is charcoal volcanic basalt/orange fissures and Moon B pale cyan ice/blue fractures when the angle includes them; neither is attached to the cabin or camera. Upper-right sunlight. Preserve complete metal geometry, no thick glass, bubble refraction, unrelated HUD, English text, logos or watermark. The authored navigation shot may contain a diegetic volumetric schematic and sparse invented glyphs, with enlarged celestial icons and compressed schematic spacing.

Edit this illustrated film frame to create the MIDDLE SCALE STATE of the same holographic navigation display. Keep Harper's exact face, freckles, curls, gray clothing, anatomy, floating pose, both hand positions, ship metal band, amber/cyan lamps, faint geodesic field, camera framing, cosmic background and solar lighting unchanged. Change ONLY the hologram's depicted contents, while keeping its physical display volume in the left/center foreground.
The display now represents a whole star system, deliberately compressed distances and enlarged symbolic body sizes, not physically accurate astronomical scale. Replace the previous dominant cloudy planet with a small but clearly recognizable turquoise/cloudy selected planet on one fine tilted orbital ellipse, with its two much tinier volcanic orange and icy blue satellites. Preserve the amber locator and tiny ship emblem at that chosen planet. A luminous soft warm-amber central star occupies the left-center of the hologram. Organize five or six other enlarged small planet icons along different compressed elliptical orbital paths around that star, some passing visibly behind others, with a restrained vertical separation cue. View the diagram obliquely as a volumetric 3D model: the orbits flatten into perspective ellipses, not a flat concentric target. The selected turquoise world must be one planet among the system, not a second giant globe in front. Keep all diagram geometry within roughly the same display bounds as the first frame. Let her selected-world marker stay near the fingertip ring via a small clean leader. Fine cyan/teal lines, a few amber highlighted nodes, sparse invented alien glyphs, no English or recognizable human digits. Clear hierarchy and plenty of air, no decorative spaghetti, no opaque screen. No real moons appear in the background. Keep painterly graphic-novel finish, no captions/logos/watermarks. This is one 16:9 shot frame, no panels or collage.

Edit the supplied illustrated film frame into the LAST SCALE STATE of the same holographic navigation display: local neighboring stars. Keep Harper's exact face, anatomy, curls, freckles, clothing, hands and floating pose, camera, ship rims/lights, cosmic background, faint field lines and warm solar lighting unchanged. Change only the contents of the hologram, within the same physical left/center display volume.
The star system has shrunk to one compact amber selected node, positioned near the fingertip selector and connected to it by the same amber leader. Within a small clean inset ring around that node retain a miniature recognizable central star and one selected turquoise planetary orbit, just enough to explain this is her HOME SYSTEM. This inset must occupy no more than 12% of the whole display's width, not still dominate it.
Fill the remaining holographic volume with an organized three-dimensional local neighborhood of 12–16 schematic star points: individual softly luminous cyan, pale blue and a few restrained warm-white star icons, scattered in real depth at several heights, nonuniform distances intentionally compressed to fit the useful display. Nearby point icons a bit larger, far ones smaller and fainter, with clear occlusion and small vertical drop-lines to an understated oblique perspective reference plane. Sparse thin cyan route connections between only selected neighboring nodes, and a few tiny alien glyph labels. This is a navigation graph in volumetric space, not a galaxy, not a spiral, not a flat star chart, not a miniature solar system full of planet balls. Remove the big planet spheres and concentric orbital ellipses of the previous scale; the only orbit trace is the tiny home-system inset. No huge visible spherical wireframe globe dominating the display. Its boundaries are implicit, with a few faint corner/reference arcs, leaving an airy cluster. The amber home-system locator is the visual continuity anchor.
Retain the graphic-novel painting, cyan holographic light on hands and face, fine lines with clear hierarchy. No recognizable English or human digits, subtitles, logos, watermark or panels. 16:9 landscape film frame. Do not add real moons outside the cabin in the background.
